correctness.rationale: For every m>=1 and 1/4<=theta<1/3, the original tree has three adopters by a strict exposure 1/4 blockade. There are exactly three initially mixed edges. Either of the two u-edges, regardless of legal S recipient, enables u and then one path/cut vertex and the whole tree; the v-edge replacement leaves v at exposure at most 1/4. Exact uniform edge sampling gives probabilities 2/3 and 1/3, with expectation 5+2m/3. The independently implemented exact-rational sample-space checker passed 60 size/threshold settings (m<=20), each enumerating all legal rewires; the all-size proof is symbolic.

value.rationale: The studied adaptation is a natural microscopic social-tie rule in the initiating literature. The result sharply separates a local apparently suppressive intervention from system-wide cascade potential: one link change, two seeds and a fixed threshold produce a full-cascade event of probability 2/3 on connected maximum-degree-four trees of unbounded size; the exact mean grows linearly. This identifies a structurally important benchmark and limitation of interpreting monotone suppression from population-average phase diagrams, rather than a routine finite slice.
